profile.campus: Secaucus / North Bergen, Hudson County, New Jersey (Equinix New York metro campus)
profile.reading:
Per Equinix own site, this NY5 facility is located at 800 Secaucus Rd, Secaucus, NJ 07094 and totals 129,436 sq ft. Redundancy: N+1 Power redundancy, N+2 Cooling redundancy; 30+ hours generator autonomy at full load. No MW power capacity figure is published on this page.

Equinix's wider New York/New Jersey metro, anchored by this Secaucus-area campus, comprised nine data centers totaling roughly 739,000 square feet of technical space as of a 2026 Data Center Frontier report, which also detailed the neighboring NY5 building's history: built in 2012 and expanded in 2016 to 20 megawatts of critical power capacity, with four utility feeder lines and eight 2.5-megawatt backup generators, and the campus remained operational for a full week without grid power during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. The campus houses matching engines for major stock-exchange electronic trading and serves financial-services firms seeking proximity to Wall Street with far more colocation space than Manhattan itself can offer; nearby NY11 in Carteret, NJ primarily serves Nasdaq and was being expanded to host an AWS Local Zone as of the same report.

Equinix, the operator, was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection provider operating more than 260 data centers across over 70 metros worldwide; the company converted to a real estate investment trust (REIT) in 2015. Within its International Business Exchange (IBX) portfolio, buildings like this one offer private cages and suites, Equinix Fabric software-defined interconnection, Internet Exchange peering, and cross-connects linking enterprises directly to cloud on-ramps for AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud.

This Secaucus/North Bergen cluster sits in Hudson County, New Jersey, roughly 10 miles from Lower Manhattan; the area's lower real estate costs and proximity to the Wall Street financial corridor, rather than any single anchor tenant, are what have concentrated Equinix's largest East Coast metro campus here rather than in New York City itself.

reading.body:
NY5 in Secaucus is one of nine facilities in Equinix's New York metro campus, occupying 129,436 square feet with N+1 power redundancy, N+2 cooling redundancy, and 30+ hours of generator autonomy at full load. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this building. According to a 2026 Data Center Frontier report, the wider Secaucus-area campus was expanded in 2016 to 20 megawatts of critical power capacity with four utility feeder lines and eight 2.5-megawatt backup generators, though whether this 20 MW figure applies to NY5 alone or the multi-building campus is not stated in the published specs.

The Secaucus campus was built to serve stock-exchange electronic trading and financial-services firms seeking Wall Street proximity without Manhattan real estate costs. It remained operational for a full week without grid power during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. Among New Jersey's 48 mapped data center facilities, only five publish megawatt figures; NY5 ranks sixth statewide by disclosed capacity, though its exact contribution to the state's published 111.3 MW total cannot be derived from available specs.

This facility qualifies to host private colocation, software-defined interconnection via Equinix Fabric, Internet Exchange peering, and cross-connects to AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud. The site's significance lies in financial and enterprise tenant density tied to East Coast trading venues, not in absolute power availability. Whether this campus can absorb substantial AI compute load depends on unpublished grid interconnect capacity and the operator's allocation priority between legacy tenants and new workloads.
